newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro stocks boosted by Wall St, strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro stocks boosted by Wall St, strong dollar.

text.p: An overnight rally on Wall Street helped lift European stocks, which were also supported on Tuesday by a stronger dollar and consequently improved export prospects.

The dollar, still in a bullish mood after encouraging comments from the recent G7 industrialised countries meeting, edged ahead further against the mark and yen, though some dealers were wary ahead of U.S. economic data due later on Tuesday.

In London, shares on the blue-chip FTSE index pushed through the 4,400-point resistance level to their highest in six weeks slightly, taking a lead from New York which on Monday ended a three-session losing streak.

Wall Street investors overcame a sell-off in Boeing shares after disappointng earnings to push the Dow Jones industrial average up 44.15 to a 6,783.02 close, and give European stocks a lift at the start.
London had also been led higher by a renewed surge in financial stocks as investment funds continued to flood into banks and insurers.
Bank shares were squeezed higher as investment funds flooded into the sector to increase weighting in anticipation of the entry into the FTSE 100 of Halifax and other former building societies.

But the market's early gains were pruned back by midday amid fresh worries about rising interest rates on both sides of the Atlantic and with many investors sitting on the sidelines ahead of Thursday's British election.

"Banks and insurers have been running quite hard and that is the real strength in the index," said a senior equity dealer at one brokerage. "But the rest of the market isn't really going anywhere and there isn't a lot of volume around."

Anxiety about higher interest rates to check inflationary pressures were renewed by a British report which showed consumer confidence at its highest since the late 1980's, even before the release of billions of pounds from a current wave of building society demutualisations.
"There are fears growing that we could be about to have a bit of a spending boom," another dealer said.
The Paris bourse was the best performer, climbing 1.33 percent by lunchtime, supported by gains in the bonds and the stronger dollar, which would help exporting sectors.
French construction firm Bouygues rose nearly four percent to 550 after a positive analysts' meeting yesterday. A broker said the stock was considered cheap on a net asset value estimated at 750

But some investors, particularly foreign funds, remained wary. They awaited the May 25-June 1 French parliamentary election, hoping for the return of a centre-right majority which will support measures to allow France to meet its Maastricht commitments and adopt more liberal economic policies.
"Then the market will go through the roof," the broker said.
Frankfurt perked up after a negative showing on Monday. The market climbed 0.6 percent, supported by the dollar and the overnight Wall Street advance.
"Despite the relatively friendly influence from Wall Street, the German market is rather sluggish," SuedwestLB said in its morning market commentary as the DAX index climbed 20.55 points to 3383.61.

On currency markets, the dollar was stronger against the mark and yen in Europe morning trade, although fluctuations were small with traders loath to move ahead of some key U.S. data due later in the day which will provide pointers on the health of the U.S. economy.

The U.S. employment cost index for the first quarter of 1997, due at 1230 GMT, should provide fresh incentive for the dollar, traders said, adding that they would also be keenly watching how U.S. Treasuries and the Dow react to the figures.
"Now that the G7 is over... the data should bring out speculation about a U.S. interest rate hike again which should be dollar-supportive," said one trader at a Japanese bank here.

"The market's waiting for confirmation from data that U.S. rates are still headed upwards. When we have that, which we probably will today, I think we'll see the dollar push on a bit further," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull in London.
After trading in a very tight range against both the mark and yen overnight, the dollar was at 1.7314 marks and 126.72 yen, up from 1.7274 and 126.61 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCKS AT 1115 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 6.8 points at 4,396.5.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 31.26 points at 2,581.51.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 19.05 at 3,382.11.
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7314 against the mark versus 1.7274 in late European trade on Friday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 126.72 from 126.61.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $338.95 after ending at $340.05 in London on Monday. Silver was at $4.64, down two cents.
